request: Plan 2 days in Lisbon for 1 people under 600 USD, with museums and food, at a fast pace. Avoid nightclubs. Use synthetic hotel quotes and leave unknown costs unpriced. Dates: 2027-04-10 through 2027-04-11. Include a park; use a fast pace and verify travel times between visits.

citations.excerpt: Lisbon's western district is packed with famous monuments, especially along the riverbank. These include the Torre de Belém, the Monument to the Discoveries, and Jerónimos Monastery. Museums include the Navy Museum, the Museu Colecção Berardo, and the National Coach Museum.

citations.title: Lisbon
citations.attribution: Content from Wikivoyage is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.
citations.excerpt: The Bairro Alto, or "Upper District" (dare we say "High Neighbourhood"), has become Lisbon's youthful, trendy quarter. The district includes the Chiado neighbourhood, known for its numerous historic landmarks and theatres. Among the district's many sights are the São Bento Palace (where the Portuguese parliament meets), the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga (a museum of antique art), and the Lisbon Botanical Gardens.

chunks.excerpt:
Lisbon (Portuguese: Lisboa) is the capital of Portugal situated on seven hills at the wide mouth of the river Tagus (Tejo) where it meets the Atlantic Ocean. chunks.attribution: Content from Wikivoyage is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.
chunks.excerpt:
All of Lisbon has 4G from all Portuguese carriers. As of Jan 2023, 5G coverage is quite broad in most popular areas. Deep inside some older buildings, or underground you might find coverage to be spotty.
Private international call centres and public telephone booths are common throughout Lisbon. Be warned, however, public phones can be less generous than slot machines: many times they'll swallow your change and give you no credit.
